mentions.name: Docules
mentions.description: A collaborative team documentation tool with no embedded AI features, focusing on being a fast, solid docs product: real-time collaboration, hierarchical docs with drag-and-drop, semantic search, comments, version history, public sharing, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and webhooks. It provides an API and a separate MCP server package exposing search, document CRUD, and comments so users can connect their own AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT. Built with React, Hono, PostgreSQL, and WebSockets.
mentions.problem: Every docs tool is adding AI auto-complete, AI summaries, and "generate a page" buttons and charging for it; Docules keeps AI out of the core product and instead lets users connect whatever AI tools they actually want via its API and MCP server.
mentions.audience: Teams looking for a documentation tool without bundled AI features
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been building a collaborative docs tool called Docules. The short version: it's a team documentation tool that doesn't have any embedded AI features.

mentions.name: Docules
mentions.description: Team documentation tool built without embedded AI features, offering real-time collaboration with live cursors, hierarchical docs with drag-and-drop, semantic search, comments, version history, public sharing, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and webhooks. Instead of built-in LLM features, it provides an open API and a separate MCP server package so teams can connect their own LLM workflows to read, search, create, and edit documents. Built with React, Hono, PostgreSQL, and WebSockets.
mentions.problem: Docs tools keep bolting on half-baked AI features like auto-complete, AI summaries, and "generate a page" buttons and charging for them; this project aims to be a solid docs tool first and let teams plug in whatever AI workflow actually makes sense for them via the open API and MCP server.
mentions.audience: Team documentation tool for teams that want a solid docs foundation and to plug in their own AI workflows.
